units.translation: 12 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Σιντηΐδα: such as: I 608. the one settled by the Sintians. This is a tyrannical (Tyrrhenian Hemsterhuis) and piratical people. Some say the Sintians are the Lemnians (Lemnioi in Etymologicum Magnum). For these, taking ships (weapons in V), harmed those passing by, that is, damaged them [whence also sinos, damage, omitted in Etymologicum Magnum]. Or because they are thought to have first invented weapons of war, which admittedly cause harm (the following from scholia on Homer omitted in B). scholia ABT on A 594, scholia on θ 294, Apollonius Lexicon Homericum 141, 25 B.
16 παρὰ instead of πρὸς in K
18 scholia A on H 468, scholia on Pindar Pythian IV 88b. 449, Apollodorus Bibliotheca I 114 sq., Hyginus Fabulae 15

When those who were at war with the Thracians and took captive concubines from there turned away from their lawful wives because of the goddess's wrath, the women voted to kill their husbands at night. And not only did they do this, but they also killed the captive women, and fearing that their sons, when grown, would seek to exact vengeance for their fathers, they killed the entire male sex together.

24 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Σίκινον: Sikinos is an island near Euboea, formerly called Oinoe (A, -oie B) because it is vine-growing. It was renamed after (the added in B) son of Thoas (the added in B) Sikinos and the nymph Oinoe the Naiad (A, daidos B). Apollonius (Etymologicum Magnum adds: and him addressed from verses 623-624). Stephanus Byzantius Σίκινος — Pliny Natural History IV 70

Of Euboea, formerly called Oinoe because it is vine-growing. Xenagoras (240 FGrH 31 J.) mentions the renaming, saying that it was renamed after Sikinos, son of Thoas and the nymph Oineis. That Thoas was saved here is recorded by both Cleon of Curium and Asclepiades of Myrlea, showing that Apollonius took everything from Cleon.
